guidance_note: When adding an async query whose result races synchronous notifications, write out the event interleavings (close during bootstrap, bootstrap during refresh, generation reuse after reset) before coding the guard, so its liveness and collision cases are designed rather than found one per review round.

evidence: TopologyEpochTracker, created by the F7 fix, inserted a `windowGens` entry per window ever seen and only incremented it on close, so the map grows without bound (slowly). b601513 switched to `windowGens.delete(windowId)`. That delete is what later let generations collide (F26).
guidance_note: When introducing a per-key map in a long-lived client, decide its eviction point in the same commit, and when evicting a generation counter make sure the next counter cannot restart at a previously issued value.

guidance_note: When migrating a single-pane consumer onto a multi-pane contract, check which state it holds per stream and either key that state by paneId or document the scope restriction.

guidance_note: When a derived index (windowIndex) drives deletes on the authoritative table, check that the table still agrees before deleting, from the first version of the code.

The F7 epoch tracker invalidated refreshes only on window-close, not when a newer bootstrap superseded them, so a stale `list-panes -t @W` could overwrite a fresh seed. d7c3f6d added `windowGens.clear()` in startBootstrap, and that clear produced the F26 collision.
guidance_note: When building an epoch guard, enumerate every event that supersedes each in-flight query type (close, bootstrap, newer refresh) and wire all of them in the first fix.

evidence: a731eba changed the code to `wc.send(IPC.paneBytes, msg)`, but the header comment and JSDoc still said `{ paneId, data }`. d7c3f6d updated the JSDoc.
guidance_note: When changing a send's payload, grep the file for the old payload literal in comments and update them in the same commit.

evidence: The F7 fix made `invalidateWindow` bump `bootstrapGen`, so a window-close during the first bootstrap discards the whole seed and no retry follows. Before, a slightly stale seed with dead panes was harmless; now session/window routing for every pane can stay empty. The agent conceded 'valid in theory', but its 'self-correcting' claim fails: pane output triggers no topology refresh. Its law objections don't hold either, since a shared helper or a 'closed during flight' set re-applied after seed would not duplicate code.
guidance_note: When an invalidation guard discards a result, check liveness as well as safety: dropping a full bootstrap needs a re-run or a reconcile (apply the seed, then re-remove windows closed in flight), not reliance on future events.

evidence: d7c3f6d, the named fix for F23, cleared `windowGens`, after which `startWindowRefresh` recomputes `(undefined ?? 0) + 1 = 1` and a stale refresh holding gen 1 validates; b601513's delete (F17) has the same flaw. e7f08b0 replaced per-window counters with one monotonic `windowEpoch`. The cited law is about types, while this fix is a value-range invariant.
guidance_note: Never reset or delete a generation counter that outstanding tokens were drawn from; draw tokens from one monotonic sequence from the start.

narrative: A large API refactor drew mostly original-code findings across 11 rounds, but two fix lineages bred follow-ups. The F3 message-loss fix touched only the WebSocket connector, so the identical Electron losses (F4/F5) and two docstrings (F6/F24) each cost later attention. The F7 race fix introduced TopologyEpochTracker, which was then patched four times: unbounded map (F17), bootstrap not superseding refreshes (F23), generation collision after the clear/delete fixes (F26), and a liveness regression (F25) that the agent pushed back on with inapt law citations. Rounds 1, 7, 8 and 9 exist only because of incomplete or wrong earlier fixes.
guidance_observations: The epoch guard was designed incrementally under review; writing the interleaving table (close/bootstrap/refresh/reset) before the first fix would have collapsed F17, F23, F25 and F26 into one change.

Law tokens were attached to fixes and pushbacks as justification (no-defensive-null-guards for exception swallowing, types-are-the-program for a counter, single-enforcer against a retry) where they did not apply.

Doc and changelog prose repeatedly lagged the code (seeded-at-connect, internal, dead design-doc path, old payload shape); a doc-vs-code pass before opening the PR would have removed about seven findings.
